challenges.title: Redact personal data before prompting
challenges.prompt: Write redact(text) that replaces email addresses with [EMAIL] and phone numbers with [PHONE] before a support ticket is pasted into an AI tool, leaving short numbers such as order ids untouched.
challenges.starter:
import re

def redact(text):
    # replace email addresses with [EMAIL] and phone numbers with [PHONE]
    # (leave short numbers such as order ids alone)
    return text

ticket = ("Hi, I'm Dana (dana.lee@example.com). Please call +1 415-555-0142 "
          "or 020 7946 0958 about order 88231.")
print(redact(ticket))
challenges.expected: Hi, I'm Dana ([EMAIL]). Please call [PHONE] or [PHONE] about order 88231.
challenges.solution:
import re

def redact(text):
    text = re.sub(r"[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[\w.]+", "[EMAIL]", text)
    text = re.sub(r"\+?\d[\d\s().-]{7,}\d", "[PHONE]", text)
    return text

ticket = ("Hi, I'm Dana (dana.lee@example.com). Please call +1 415-555-0142 "
          "or 020 7946 0958 about order 88231.")
print(redact(ticket))
challenges.explain: Minimizing what goes into a prompt is the first privacy habit. A regex isn't a complete PII detector (names and addresses need other tools), but it's a cheap, testable first filter. Verified by running the solution.

challenges.title: Score two prompt versions on a test set
challenges.prompt: Implement passes() (under 40 words, contains the required keyword, no banned phrase) and pass_rate_v(index). Compare prompt versions v1 and v2 on the test set and list regressions, the cases that passed with v1 but fail with v2.
challenges.starter:
# Each test case: (name, output_from_prompt_v1, output_from_prompt_v2). The rubric checks
# that an answer is under 40 words, contains a required keyword and has no banned phrase.
CASES = [
    ("refund",   "We will refund you within 5 days. Sorry for the trouble.", "Refund issued. It arrives within 5 days."),
    ("shipping", "Your parcel ships Monday and arrives Wednesday.", "Probably ships soon, I think."),
    ("outage",   "As an AI I cannot confirm an outage; check the status page.", "Check the status page for outage updates."),
]
REQUIRED = {"refund": "refund", "shipping": "ships", "outage": "status page"}
BANNED = ["as an ai", "i think", "probably"]

def passes(name, text):
    # True when text is under 40 words, contains REQUIRED[name] and none of BANNED
    return False

def pass_rate_v(index):
    # share of CASES whose output at tuple position `index` passes
    return 0.0

v1, v2 = pass_rate_v(1), pass_rate_v(2)
print("v1: %.0f%%" % (v1 * 100))
print("v2: %.0f%%" % (v2 * 100))
print("failing in v2:", [c[0] for c in CASES if not passes(c[0], c[2])])
print("regressions:", [c[0] for c in CASES if passes(c[0], c[1]) and not passes(c[0], c[2])])
challenges.expected:
v1: 67%
v2: 67%
failing in v2: ['shipping']
regressions: ['shipping']
challenges.solution:
# Each test case: (name, output_from_prompt_v1, output_from_prompt_v2). The rubric checks
# that an answer is under 40 words, contains a required keyword and has no banned phrase.
CASES = [
    ("refund",   "We will refund you within 5 days. Sorry for the trouble.", "Refund issued. It arrives within 5 days."),
    ("shipping", "Your parcel ships Monday and arrives Wednesday.", "Probably ships soon, I think."),
    ("outage",   "As an AI I cannot confirm an outage; check the status page.", "Check the status page for outage updates."),
]
REQUIRED = {"refund": "refund", "shipping": "ships", "outage": "status page"}
BANNED = ["as an ai", "i think", "probably"]

def passes(name, text):
    t = text.lower()
    return (len(text.split()) < 40
            and REQUIRED[name] in t
            and not any(b in t for b in BANNED))

def pass_rate(version):
    results = [passes(name, outs[version]) for name, *outs in CASES]
    return sum(results) / len(results)

def pass_rate_v(index):
    return sum(passes(c[0], c[index]) for c in CASES) / len(CASES)

v1, v2 = pass_rate_v(1), pass_rate_v(2)
print("v1: %.0f%%" % (v1 * 100))
print("v2: %.0f%%" % (v2 * 100))
print("failing in v2:", [c[0] for c in CASES if not passes(c[0], c[2])])
print("regressions:", [c[0] for c in CASES if passes(c[0], c[1]) and not passes(c[0], c[2])])
challenges.explain: Both versions score 67%, yet v2 fixed the outage case while breaking shipping. Equal averages can hide regressions, which is why you re-run the whole test set and compare per case. Verified by running the solution.
